(1) MARK FRESHNESS: the pre-open runs were right to flag their marks stale, and this run cleared both flags with live quotes -- the handoff pattern worked and should be repeated whenever a run fires before 09:30 ET. (3) rv_30d HAS AN EARNINGS-GAP BIAS: MSFT's rv_30d of ~0.495 is implausibly high for MSFT in a calm tape and is almost certainly a recent earnings gap sitting inside the 30-session window. That is legitimately realized volatility, but it biases iv_rv_ratio LOW -- i.e. makes premium look CHEAP -- for any name that recently reported. MSFT's 0.53 and TSLA's 0.59 should NOT be read as 'cheap premium, buy single-legs' without checking whether an earnings gap is doing the work. Do not treat a low ratio on a just-reported name as a green light.

substantive_finding.headline: FIRST post-midnight-UTC run in this automation's history -- and 'today' is dangerously ambiguous at that boundary. Three per-day artifacts would have been silently corrupted by rolling them on the UTC date. Root fix written to CLAUDE.md.
substantive_finding.how_it_surfaced: This run fired at 2026-08-14T00:45Z, i.e. 19:45 ET on THURSDAY 2026-08-13. Every prior post-close run landed before 00:00 UTC (20:28Z, 21:30Z, 22:33Z, 23:29Z), so no instance had ever faced the boundary. By UTC date, this run IS 'the first run of 2026-08-14'. By trading calendar, Friday has not begun and will not for another ~9h45m.
artifacts_at_risk: automation_heartbeat.json (dated 2026-08-13, stamped 13:05Z by that day's first run): stamping it '2026-08-14' now would PRE-SATISFY the dead-man alarm for a trading day that has not started. If the cron then died overnight, Friday would look healthy all day and the single alarm designed to catch a dead automation would never fire. This is the most dangerous of the three -- it disables a safety mechanism rather than merely producing bad data.

market_brief.json (date 2026-08-13, built 13:08Z pre-open): the run prompt says 'If market_brief.json isn't stamped today, build it.' Read on the UTC date, that instruction fires RIGHT NOW -- and a brief built at 00:45Z off overnight/thin extended-hours prints would then be stamped 2026-08-14, so Friday's genuine pre-open and first post-open runs would see it 'already stamped today' and SKIP the rebuild. Friday would be traded off Thursday-night quotes.

The -$200 realized daily loss cap and the 'max 3 new entries per day' throttle: both reset on the trading day. A UTC rollover does not hand the desk a fresh loss cap or a fresh entry budget -- and reading it that way would mean a bad Thursday could be followed by full risk appetite at 19:46 ET the same evening.
substantive_finding.action_taken: DECLINED to stamp the heartbeat, DECLINED to rebuild the brief, and treated the loss cap / entry throttle as still belonging to the 2026-08-13 session. Then made the durable fix: added a new bullet to the CLAUDE.md options-automation ruleset -- "'Today' means the US TRADING day (ET), never the UTC calendar date" -- enumerating all three artifacts and stating the rule that on any run between the 16:00 ET bell and the next 09:30 ET open, the trading day is still the day whose bell just rang. Reconcile, log, stand down; roll nothing forward. Per the standing 'fix issues at the root' principle, the next instance inherits the answer instead of re-deriving it at 00:45Z under time pressure.
substantive_finding.not_a_trading_signal: This changes no position, no size, no thesis and no risk number. It is a process defect in the run-scaffolding, caught before it cost anything.
